PR: Ability to identify recurring patterns, trends, or sequences within a given set of data or materials (e.g., detecting similarities in a sequence of numbers or text).
CA: Ability to form abstract concepts or categories based on shared characteristics or relationships among a set of materials.
HP: Ability to propose plausible explanations or predictions for incomplete information (e.g., inferring causes of a fictional conflict, suggesting scientific hypotheses).
RG: Ability to start with stated rules, premises, or conditions, and to engage in one or more steps to reach a solution to a novel problem.
RQ: Ability to inductively and deductively reason with concepts involving mathematical relations and properties.
CM: Ability to mimic speak in real-life situations (e.g., lecture, group participation) in an adult-like manner.
RD: Ability to recognize and decode words or pseudowords in reading.
WA: Ability to write with clarity of thought, organization, and good sentence structure.
NA: Ability to rapidly produce names for concepts when presented with a text cue.
FA: Ability to rapidly produce a series of original or useful ideas related to a particular concept.
FE: Ability to rapidly think of different ways of expressing an idea.
SP: Ability to rapidly think of a number of solutions to particular practical problem.
FO: Ability to rapidly produce original, clever, and insightful responses (expressions, interpretations) to a given topic, situation, or task.
FI: Ability to rapidly produce a series of ideas, words, or phrases related to a specific condition or object. Quantity, not quality, is emphasized.
FW: Ability to rapidly produce words that have specific phonemic, structural, or orthographic characteristics (independent of word meanings).
